terra.reason: A documented port override can be lost when launching the deploy job, causing it to contact the wrong port and fail or affect another daemon.

sonnet.reason: Raw deploy output goes to a local 0700 log file unredacted, so a credential printed by the deploy would be stored in clear text. The deploy CLI already redacts its gate output and the log route does not serve this path, so this is unlikely.

terra.reason: A credential printed by a deployment command is persisted in the log without redaction.

sonnet.reason: After an SSE reconnect the Land page shows stale rows for at most 15 seconds, until the next poll corrects it.

terra.reason: After a connection interruption, the Land page can show stale information until its next poll, at most 15 seconds later.

terra.reason: On an unsupported deployment platform, the configuration error is reported at deploy time rather than at startup.

sonnet.reason: A restart during a rate-limit wait only causes an early extra poll that is rate-limited again and waits again, with no lost work or wrong result.

terra.reason: A restart during a rate-limit cooldown causes an early poll and another wait, generating avoidable requests without changing the demonstrated gate result.

sonnet.reason: Lenient launchctl inspection can treat a still-loaded executor as stopped (letting checkout change under it) or as not loaded in uninstall/status, but it needs launchctl to be killed, to time out, or to hit a permission error after printing the exact missing-service text, which real launchctl does not do in normal operation.

terra.reason: An abnormal service inspection can be mistaken for confirmed absence, allowing deployment or uninstallation to proceed while the executor remains loaded and potentially disrupting or wasting its work.

sonnet.reason: A reference-style link or autolink with a local-looking `#N` is misparsed into a wrong advisory 'ready for acceptance' feed item. The parser only reads trusted-author bodies, the factory takes no action on the item, and the input is contrived.

terra.reason: Reference-style links or autolinks can make the advisory feed falsely report acceptance readiness or miss a valid reference, potentially prompting a wasted review or delaying attention.

sonnet.reason: A reproduced failure to inspect the old daemon after a successful drain leaves the scheduler paused with no resume, so no new runs start until someone resumes it by hand; this needs a transient launchctl inspection error at that moment.

terra.reason: A service inspection failure after draining leaves the daemon paused and unable to start new work until an operator resumes it.

sonnet.reason: An executor label collision or an inspection failure is reported only after the daemon has been replaced, so install exits non-zero with an avoidable restart; the daemon is replaced with a working unit and the executor is untouched, and the base code already ordered checks this way.

terra.reason: An executor collision or inspection failure can make installation fail after replacing the daemon, leaving a partial installation that requires operator intervention.

sonnet.reason: Only the test's baseline is weak because it shares the adapter, with no runtime defect at head, and a regression would need a future change to the adapter.

terra.reason: The current adapter behaves correctly, but the comparison can miss a plausible future notification regression because both sides use the same adapter.

sonnet.reason: No test checks that ctx.run is refreshed after a stage write, but the production assignment is correct at head, so the gap only matters if a later change removes it.

terra.reason: The current engine correctly refreshes its in-memory run, but the tests can miss a plausible future regression that leaves stage callbacks with stale values.

sonnet.reason: Two processes racing to initialize the member identity on a fresh database can return and then change distinct identities (reproduced), but it needs a simultaneous first open and nothing outside tests calls it yet.

terra.reason: Concurrent initialization can overwrite the persisted member identity, leaving one process with an identity that changes after restart.

sonnet.reason: Concurrent writes with different abort signals send duplicate tree and repository requests (reproduced), but both writes succeed with identical correct results, so the only cost is extra API calls.

terra.reason: Concurrent writes with distinct cancellation signals issue redundant API requests while both writes still succeed.

sonnet.reason: The clock-skew test covers only creates, so a clock-dependent regression in renewals or releases would go undetected, but the current implementation behaves correctly.

terra.reason: The required clock-skew coverage misses renewal and release cases, but the current implementation has no demonstrated clock-dependent runtime defect.

sonnet.reason: Both adjudicators reproduced that lowercasing the configured name misses the case-sensitive lookup, so queue-started runs attach to a duplicate repository record with the wrong default merge policy, which is wasted or wrong work when the saved name has capitals.

terra.reason: A mixed-case repository name can cause queue runs to use a duplicate record with the default merge policy instead of the owner's saved policy.

sonnet.reason: The unfiltered per-poll scan of all runs and prompts adds a history-dependent synchronous stall (about 20 ms at 3000 runs), but results stay correct and the work is only delayed.

terra.reason: Every poll synchronously scans run history, adding a growing responsiveness pause, but the reproduced delays do not establish lost work or an outage.

sonnet.reason: Consecutive section-reference lines (a format the issue cites from prior tickets) cause the second section's requirements to be silently dropped, so a run can succeed without assessing them.

terra.reason: Consecutive section references are a cited ticket format, and dropping the second can allow success without assessing its requirements.

sonnet.reason: A heading inside a collapsed <details> block at the same level as the referenced section truncates it, silently dropping later requirements, but this needs an uncommon document layout.

terra.reason: A heading inside a collapsed details block can truncate a referenced section and leave later requirements unchecked.

sonnet.reason: Prose that merely mentions a section is treated as a reference and adds unwanted requirements, so a fully assessed run ends needs_human instead of succeeded (fails closed, a refused run with real cost).

terra.reason: A prose sentence mentioning a section can add unintended requirements and send an otherwise complete run to human review.

sonnet.reason: Required numbered test cases are missing from the suite; there is no runtime effect.

terra.reason: The specified regression cases are missing, although the adjudicators identified no corresponding runtime defect.

sonnet.reason: The fixture line starting with test.skip trips the diff audit's test-skipped block, which stops delivery until the fixture is reworded; this is a reproducible workaround-able delivery hiccup, not a runtime defect.

terra.reason: The reproduced diff audit flags the fixture as a skipped test and blocks delivery during the normal audit.

sonnet.reason: A restart after journaling an unchanged renewal makes recovery report it as applied though GitHub never received it, so the manager acts on a renewal that never happened (a restart at the wrong moment, and renewals normally leave the record unchanged).

terra.reason: A restart before an unchanged renewal is sent can make recovery report it as applied, causing the manager to act on a renewal that never occurred.

sonnet.reason: Recovery treats any moved tip, including a malformed one or a same-owner write, as supersession, marks the lease lost and clears the release intent, which discards the pending final status and checkpoint. This needs a malformed or same-owner write to land at the replay moment.

terra.reason: A moved tip from the same owner or a malformed record can cause recovery to clear the durable release intent, losing its pending final status and checkpoint.

sonnet.reason: Only the diagnostic failure class (unclassified vs flaky) is mislabeled, and only when a restart lands between recording and checkpointing a post-merge failure.

terra.reason: A restart between failure recording and checkpointing can misclassify a flaky post-merge check, leading defect analysis to a wrong conclusion.

sonnet.reason: The slow_regression diagnostic flag is lost only when a restart hits that narrow window, and the check result itself is unaffected.

terra.reason: A restart at the checkpoint boundary can cause the stored observation to lose its slow-regression diagnostic flag.

sonnet.reason: A confined targeted retry blocks the land correctly but is recorded as a code regression, so a person or the factory acts on a misclassified infrastructure fault.

terra.reason: A confinement failure on a targeted retry is recorded as a code regression, potentially directing investigation toward the wrong cause.

sonnet.reason: After a release whose response is lost (or an ambiguous unchanged), the old holder's write window stays open while another coordinator holds the next generation, so the lease's write-confinement guard can be bypassed; reproduced by both adjudicators.

terra.reason: A lost release response can leave the former owner's write window open after a successor acquires the lease, breaking the ownership boundary.

sonnet.reason: After a daemon restart, recovered held leases are not in the renewal loop's handle map and go unrenewed (reproduced), so ownership can expire mid-work unless the caller acquires again.

terra.reason: After restart, restored active leases are omitted from renewal and can expire if the caller relies on the renewal loop without reacquiring.

sonnet.reason: A stale pending acquisition from a failed run makes the next run's acquire return a definitive 'refused: live' without reconciling, which causes a stuck or refused run on a still-unclaimed ref (reproduced).

terra.reason: An unapplied pending acquisition after a network failure causes a later run to be refused without reconciling the available claim.

sonnet.reason: The mutant test cases invert their assertions so they pass instead of failing, which is a test-only gap with no runtime effect.

terra.reason: The mutant test cases pass because they change the assertions, leaving the requested invariant demonstration missing without establishing a runtime defect.

sonnet.reason: Both adjudicators reproduced that mutating the recovery fixtures to capture identity after construction still passes all tests, and the defect is only missing test coverage with no runtime effect.

terra.reason: The existing tests fail to detect a plausible future regression that captures lease identity after recovery, but no current runtime defect is demonstrated.

sonnet.reason: Both adjudicators reproduced that a cancel landing after the body download on a damaged object gives a corrupt/unsupported error instead of aborted, but the read fails either way, nothing is returned or changed, and it needs a narrow timing window plus a damaged object.

terra.reason: A narrowly timed cancellation combined with an invalid object reports a validation error instead of cancellation, while the read still fails without returning data or changing state.

sonnet.reason: When the browser fails at runtime after a successful launch configuration, a blocked browser check is converted to unclear, so the bounded environment retry is skipped and the implementer receives feedback for an infrastructure failure, which wastes work and feedback rounds; it needs a runtime browser failure, which is realistic but not the default.

terra.reason: A browser runtime failure can be misclassified as an implementation problem, skipping the environment retry and wasting feedback rounds on changes that cannot fix the infrastructure.

sonnet.reason: Both adjudicators reproduced that an accepted comment is never recovered and the checkpoint is closed as done with no comment ID, so the record is wrong. This needs a lost POST response plus an unreadable private-strings file at restart, and the leak of configured private text into logs needs a transport error that contains such text, so both are contrived.

terra.reason: A publication transport error can place a configured private string in daemon logs, leaking private data under a realistic error condition.

sonnet.reason: The replay path for a retained attempt skips the binding check the change claims to add, so a saved pass is accepted despite a changed or missing binding. This needs corrupted or legacy persisted state, because the run id already fixes the repository. The other two defects, the masked original failure and a contradictory record treated as a setup failure, are smaller and stay blocked or fail.

terra.reason: After a restart, a saved passing gate result can be replayed despite a changed or missing execution binding, allowing the factory to act on verification that does not match the current run.
